projects.title: Mini-game hybrid monetization: rewarded video first, IAP and subscriptions second
projects.what: A systematic teardown of WeChat/Douyin mini-game monetization: light games lean on rewarded video (placed at out-of-energy, level-failed and double-reward moments), mid-core games add IAP plus monthly cards / Battle Pass, with each platform's revenue share and benchmark data

projects.timeCost: Prototype validation about 1-2 weeks per game; after launch, daily data checks to tune ad placements and payment points

projects.title: Cautionary tale: 623 AI-mass-produced tool sites zeroed by Google
projects.what: The author mass-produced 623 browser mini tools × 5 languages with an AI pipeline, monetized only by AdSense; after the March 2026 spam update and the May core update, traffic fell off a cliff twice. The post-mortem proves generic tool mass-production unit economics never worked; the only survivor was a creative tool with repeat visits (the ita-bag simulator)
projects.moneyLogic: The original idea was massive tool pages eating search traffic for ad money, but search demand per tool is near zero — 498 monthly clicks was the ceiling
projects.incomeEvidence: Author's own Search Console data: a peak of 498 clicks in 28 days, post-crash ad revenue about $0.07/day; the surviving ita-bag simulator got 48 clicks in 90 days at an average rank of 1.4
projects.cost: About $10 in domains + about $100/month in AI subscriptions (which the author already used for other projects)
projects.timeCost: Near-fully automated pipeline; one person running 600+ tools × 5 languages
projects.risks: This is the risk itself: templated AI mass production is the bullseye of Google's spam updates; all tools share one Google traffic river and one update wipes them all out; verify what a single tool can earn before scaling
projects.firstStep: Today: take your own mass-production tool list and compute the monthly clicks and revenue ceiling of just the first tool before deciding to scale
projects.matchReason: Highly relevant to the user's batch content-production pipelines with free/paid models — a must-read stop-loss checklist before building tool sites

warnings.title: Luxury Consignment Platforms Like Feiyu: Unpaid-Seller Lawsuit Opens, Payouts Can Drag Past 60 Days
warnings.reason: Feiyu's case over unpaid seller funds opened in court in 2026, involving hundreds of consignment sellers and tens of millions of yuan in payments; the core dispute is the payout cycle and the platform's cash flow. Consignment commission is 22%–25% excluding warehousing and return shipping, normal payouts take about 45 days, and review delays or returns can stretch them past 60 days; unpopular items can sit unsold for six months while warehousing fees keep accruing. There is also 'arrival price-cutting', where buyers haggle down the price after receiving the item — a related case was ruled on by the Beijing Fengtai Court in March 2026.
